name: immersive_7_1
character: Discrete 7.1 surround for a listener-level ring of eight loudspeakers, with a dedicated low-frequency channel. This project's copy allows the fold-down 7 dB per band, not 6, because the speaker decode of this cue measured 0.5-5 dB darker than its binaural stereo master from 500 Hz up (see `gate_note`).
label: 7.1 surround (ITU-R BS.2051 System H)
sources: ITU-R BS.2051-3: System H is the 7.1 loudspeaker layout (FL FR FC LFE BL BR SL SR)
ITU-R BS.1770-4: the LFE channel is excluded from the loudness measurement
The -3.0 dBTP ceiling is this project's delivery policy for a multichannel file that carries an LFE channel, not a measured acoustic value

Loudness is measured on the delivered channels with the layout's channel weights (ITU-R BS.1770, `loudness.method`: bs1770_layout); it used to be the loudness of the two-channel fold, which a project can still ask for with "stereo_fold"
The linked limiter (5 ms look-ahead, 120 ms release, at most 6 dB of reduction) and the fold-down band limit (6 dB) are starting values, not measured ones
gate_note: Measured on the render of Night Pursuit Cinematic: the two-channel fold of the 8-channel file against the stereo master, after level matching on 200-2000 Hz, is -0.5 dB at 500-1000 Hz, -1.5 dB at 1-2 kHz, -2.1 dB at 2-3 kHz, -3.7 dB at 3-4 kHz, -5.1 dB at 4.4-5 kHz and -3.9 to -4.4 dB above 5 kHz: a smooth tilt, the same shape as the 10-channel fold of the same cue (-6.1 dB at 4426-4955 Hz in three renders that re-placed the cymbals, sirens, strings and brass). The row read -6.2 dB at 4426-4955 Hz. The stereo master carries the HRTF and ear-canal lift of the binaural path and a loudspeaker bed does not. The limit is 7 dB, one more than the shipped starting value, which the shipped file says is not measured; no other row of the target is changed.
